title: Every panel follows the design system
goal: The video panels had no side margins and each invented its own layout, and nothing compares panels against the design rules. Check every panel against those rules and fix what does not follow them.
notes:
Intake detail (the goal as first filed, moved here by triage 2026-09-23): The four video inspectors had no horizontal inset and invented their own layouts; nothing compared panels to UX-PATTERNS. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask throughout: would a Premiere editor get this, and is it easier here?

Filed from the 2026-09-23 video audit in the intake window.
acceptance: Every inspector section in Sources/Photonz is checked for panelEdgeInset, row layout, control height, typography and control choice (dropdown vs radio) against UX-PATTERNS and the mock CSS
Offenders fixed where small, filed where not, with pictures

log.note: triage 2026-09-23: goal rewritten in plain language, the old one kept at the top of notes

video-shell.html was deleted on 2026-09-23 (task the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is): it was the loop's own study arguing against tracks. The target is now pages/video.html, the video-*.html walkthroughs and comp-video.html, restored as the user drew them, plus UX-PATTERNS D18 (rewritten: a document with time has tracks). Where this task mentions video-shell, read video.html.

Review before building: the video sections the user complained about were already fixed by the-video-properties-look-like-the-rest-of-the-d; what was missing was anything that COMPARES a panel to the rules. Reading 40 section views by eye cannot settle where a row lands, so the check had to be a measurement of the running app, at defaults, at the default and the narrowest dock.

Built: PanelMarginRule (PhotonzCore, 16 tests): every row/control keeps the 14pt margin both sides, and the panel is no wider than its dock (SwiftUI centres a too-wide section, so one rigid row slides EVERY section over the canvas). New walk step panelMargins (reads the PanelTargetView register plus accessibility frames, never names; report:true to survey) and action dockNarrowest (220pt, restored in finish()). Surveyed 9 picture states, 25 video states, tools, Library and components. Found and fixed: (1) a screen picked made the panel 276pt in a 264 dock: ArrangementInspector.row's HStack(spacing 8)+Spacer(min 8) made the least gap 24pt, and its segmented controls were regular size where every other panel segmented control is small; now small, one line when it fits, label-over-control when not (ViewThatFits). (2) captions made the panel 265.5-267pt: the system segmented Style bar cannot shrink below its words; new VideoKit.Segmented (the mock's .seg.fill.sm: natural widths plus an equal share, a raised plate that slides, a VideoKit.Dropdown when the words do not fit) for Style and Position. (3) Library shelf used its own 12pt inset: now panelEdgeInset; its scope bar made the narrowest dock 30pt too wide: now VideoKit.Segmented (walks press segments by name through a new kitControl seam). (4) Narrowest dock: Animating rows read 'P' for Position and px wrapped: rows drop the value under the name, units fixedSize. Control choice: no radio columns anywhere in the panel; every exclusive list over three options is already a dropdown.

Review after, on the probe at defaults: every-panel-keeps-its-margins-walk (10 states incl. 220pt dock and Library) and captions-panel-keeps-its-margins-walk (4 states) pass with strict panelMargins; strict steps also added to video-panel-order-walk (clip, title, sound) and transition-picker-at-a-cut-walk (dissolve). 40 walks touching arrangement, library, captions and Animating pass; keys-copy-between-layers-walk fails at step 77 exactly as in the 2026-09-24 08:57 sweep (owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-5). Filed: panel-row-labels-are-one-size-and-sit-in-one-col (p1, picture sections use 12pt stacked labels where the mock and video sections use 10.5pt in a 76pt column), the-captions-section-says-every-button-and-colou (p2, 'Write Ag...' and '#000000B3'). Left rough, not filed (no edge crossed, only tight): at 220pt Canvas's button reads 'Ca...' and Language 'English (e...'. panelMargins is not yet watched under a lock, so it is refused there by default. A mistaken task no-placeholder-task was created by a botched dry run and dropped at once.
